finding.claim: Claim validators are skipped when the claim is absent, so allowedAud/allowedIss/allowedSub/allowedJti/allowedNonce and maxAge are not enforced for tokens that omit the claim, unless requiredClaims lists them. Severity medium (conditional).
finding.source: Token payload. The attacker needs a token that passes the signature check and omits aud, iss, sub, jti, nonce, or iat (for maxAge). Requires the same signing key to issue tokens lacking those claims, e.g. a key shared across audiences or services, or an issuer that emits tokens without iat.
finding.sink: Authorization decision that relies on allowedAud / allowedIss / maxAge being enforced (validator loop at verifier.js:304-323).

trace.note: allowed* options become validators that run only when the claim is present (604-638)
requiredClaims is the only mandatory-claim gate, and it is optional (293-298)
for each validator, `if (!(claim in payload)) continue`
maxAge validator uses claim 'iat', so it is skipped when iat is missing (616-618)

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified first (verifier.js:280) proves only that the trusted key signed the token. Type checks (verifier.js:316) run only on present claims. No default requiredClaims. Likely intended upstream design, but a footgun for verifiers relying on audience or issuer binding without requiredClaims.

finding.claim: Signature segment is validated only for base64url alphabet, not canonical encoding. Trailing unused bits in the last character decode to the same bytes, so one signature has several distinct token strings that all verify. ECDSA also accepts high-S signatures. The comment at verifier.js:166-168 says the signature is canonical at that point, which is false. Severity low.
finding.source: Attacker holds any valid token and edits the last character of its signature segment.
finding.sink: Any consumer that keys revocation, one-time-use, or replay tracking on the raw token string.

trace.note: signature checked only with that regex (41-43)
verifySignature called on the raw signature
timingSafeEqual compares decoded bytes, so variants verify

finding.guards_checked: Header and payload segments are not affected: the signature covers the raw 'header.payload' string (verifier.js:397-398). Signature length enforced by timingSafeEqual (wrong length returns false, crypto.js:301). Cache keys hash the whole token string (utils.js:45-58), so a variant gets a cache miss, not a bypass. Impact exists only if the application uses the raw token string for denylist or replay control.

finding.claim: With cache enabled and a token that has exp but no iat, the cache entry lifetime ignores exp and uses cacheTTL (default 600000 ms). An expired token is accepted from cache for up to cacheTTL after exp. Severity low.
finding.source: A token carrying exp but omitting iat. Needs an issuer that uses noTimestamp or otherwise omits iat, plus a verifier with cache enabled.
finding.sink: Cache-hit success path (verifier.js:368-378) returning the payload for an expired token.

trace.note: exp only folded into cacheValue[2] inside the hasIat branch (120-129)
without iat, cacheValue[2] stays 0 and becomes now + clockTolerance + cacheTTL (133-134)
cache hit accepted while now <= max, with no exp recheck (364-375)

finding.guards_checked: Cache disabled by default (verifier.js:83-86 with undefined size; verifier.js:580). Exp enforced on first verification (verifier.js:319-321). Tokens with iat are bounded correctly by min(exp, maxTTL) (verifier.js:125-134). Requires an issuer that omits iat.

finding.claim: With caching enabled, a Buffer token reaches hashToken(), which calls token.split(). Buffer has no split method, so every verify call with a Buffer token throws a TypeError instead of a TokenError. Severity low (fail-closed).
finding.source: Caller passes a Buffer token (accepted by verifier.js:353).
finding.sink: Verification entry point: verifier.js:364 calls cacheKeyBuilder(token) before decoding.

trace.note: token.split('.', 1) on a Buffer throws TypeError

finding.guards_checked: Fails closed (no acceptance). Triggers only when cache is enabled. Could cause an unexpected 500 or crash if the caller does not catch it.

finding.claim: In the async key-function path with complete:true, `input` is set to the full token including the signature. The sync path (line 426) returns the signing input (header.payload). Consumers re-verifying with `input` get different results depending on the path. Severity low (informational).
finding.source: Caller uses complete:true with a key function.
finding.sink: Application code consuming the returned `input` field.
finding.guards_checked: Library verification itself is unaffected. Only relevant if application code uses `input` directly.
